23832-summerfield-or-life-on-a-farm.title: Life on a Farm
23832-summerfield-or-life-on-a-farm.creator: Day Kellogg Lee
23832-summerfield-or-life-on-a-farm.description: A book by Day Kellogg Lee. This object the author successfully accomplishes. No reader can arise from a perusal of his pages, without feeling a higher respect for such pursuits as benefit the world, and a stronger inclination to avoid the more showy and worthless callings into which too many are disposed to crowd. The story is most happily conceived, and is narrated in a style highly finished and attractive. There is nothing insipid or over-wrought, in the frame-work or filling up; but all is natural and lifelike.

arxiv-1403-0796.title: Organelle morphogenesis by active remodeling
arxiv-1403-0796.creator: N. Ramakrishnan 1,2, John H. Ipsen 3, Madan Rao 4,5, P. B. Sunil Kumar 1
arxiv-1403-0796.description: Abstract Intracellular organelles are subject to a steady flux of lipids and proteins through active, energy consuming transport processes. Active fission and fusion are promoted by GTPases, e.g., Arf-Coatamer and the Rab-Snare complexes, which both sense and generate local membrane curvature.

arxiv-1902-09487.title: MUREL: Multimodal Relational Reasoning for Visual Question Answering
arxiv-1902-09487.creator: Remi Cadene, Hedi Ben-younes, Matthieu Cord, Nicolas Thome
arxiv-1902-09487.description: Abstract Multimodal attentional networks are currently state-of-the-art models for Visual Question Answering (VQA) tasks involving real images. Although attention allows to focus on the visual content relevant to the question, this simple mechanism is arguably insufficient to model complex reasoning features required for VQA or other high-level tasks.

arxiv-2111-10233.title: Xp-GAN: Unsupervised Multi-object Controllable Video Generation
arxiv-2111-10233.creator: 1 st Bahman Rouhani, 2 nd Mohammad Rahmati
arxiv-2111-10233.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by 1 st Bahman Rouhani, 2 nd Mohammad Rahmati. Video Generation is a relatively new and yet popular subject in machine learning due to its vast variety of potential applications and its numerous challenges. Current methods in Video Generation provide the user with little or no control over the exact specification of how the objects in the generate video are to be moved and located at each frame, that is, the user can’t explicitly control how each object in the video should move.

arxiv-2207-09750.title: Fair Context-Aware Privacy Threat Modelling
arxiv-2207-09750.creator: Saswat Das, Rakshit Naidu
arxiv-2207-09750.description: Abstract Given the progressive nature of the world today, fairness is a very important social aspect in various areas, and it has long been studied with the advent of technology. To the best of our knowledge, methods of quantifying fairness errors and fairness in privacy threat models have been absent.

arxiv-2209-12059.title: Edge and corner superconductivity in a 2D topological model
arxiv-2209-12059.creator: Ying Wang, Gautam Rai, Stephan Haas, Anuradha Jagannathan
arxiv-2209-12059.description: Abstract We consider a two-dimensional generalization of the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model which is known to possess a non-trivial topological band structure. For this model, which is characterized by a single parameter, the hopping ratio 0 ≤ r ≤ 1 0\leq r\leq 1 , the inhomogeneous superconducting phases induced by an attractive U U Hubbard interaction are studied using mean field theory.

arxiv-2209-13751.title: New Window on Matter-Antimatter Differences from BESIII
arxiv-2209-13751.creator: Xiaorong Zhou, Stephen Lars Olsen
arxiv-2209-13751.description: Abstract Recent measurements of C ​ P CP -related comparisons of the weak-interaction parameters that describe the decays of the Ξ − \Xi^{-} and the Ξ ¯ + \bar{\Xi}^{+} doubly strange hyperon and antihyperon are reviewed and their significance is discussed. keywords J/\psi meson, Strange hyperons, CP violation PACS PACS numbers: † † catchline: Vol. , No.

arxiv-2308-09958.title: A Comparison of Adversarial Learning Techniques for Malware Detection
arxiv-2308-09958.creator: Pavla Louthánová, Matouš Kozák, Martin Jureček, Mark Stamp
arxiv-2308-09958.description: Abstract Machine learning has proven to be a useful tool for automated malware detection, but machine learning models have also been shown to be vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This article addresses the problem of generating adversarial malware samples, specifically malicious Windows Portable Executable files. We summarize and compare work that has focused on adversarial machine learning for malware detection.

arxiv-2310-17015.title: Data Augmentation for Emotion Detection in Small Imbalanced Text Data
arxiv-2310-17015.creator: Anna Koufakou, Diego Grisales, Ragy Costa de jesus, Oscar Fox
arxiv-2310-17015.description: Abstract Emotion recognition in text, the task of identifying emotions such as joy or anger, is a challenging problem in NLP with many applications. One of the challenges is the shortage of available datasets that have been annotated with emotions. Certain existing datasets are small, follow different emotion taxonomies and display imbalance in their emotion distribution.

arxiv-2403-09815.title: One-shot Learning for MIPs with SOS1 Constraints
arxiv-2403-09815.creator: Charly Robinson La Rocca, Jean-François Cordeau, Emma Frejinger
arxiv-2403-09815.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Charly Robinson La Rocca, Jean-François Cordeau, Emma Frejinger. Efficient algorithms and solvers are required to provide optimal or near-optimal solutions quickly and enable organizations to react promptly to dynamic situations such as supply chain disruptions or changing customer demands. State-of-the-art mixed-integer programming (MIP) solvers are crafted to tackle a wide variety of problems, yet many real-world situations are characterized by problem instances that originate from a narrow distribution. This has inspired the creation of tailored approaches that exploit historical data to inform heuristic design.

arxiv-2404-03803.title: Scaling of quantum Fisher information for quantum exceptional point sensors
arxiv-2404-03803.creator: Chun-Hui Liu, Fu Li, Shengwang Du, Jianming Wen, Lan Yang, Chuanwei Zhang
arxiv-2404-03803.description: Abstract In recent years, significant progress has been made in utilizing the divergence of spectrum response rate at the exceptional point (EP) for sensing in classical systems, while the use and characterization of quantum EPs for sensing have been largely unexplored.

arxiv-2406-03816.title: ReST-MCTS ∗ : LLM Self-Training via Process Reward Guided Tree Search
arxiv-2406-03816.creator: Dan Zhang, Sining Zhoubian, Ziniu Hu, Yisong Yue, Yuxiao Dong, Jie Tang
arxiv-2406-03816.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Dan Zhang, Sining Zhoubian, Ziniu Hu, Yisong Yue, Yuxiao Dong, Jie Tang. Recent methodologies in LLM self-training mostly rely on LLM generating responses and filtering those with correct output answers as training data. This approach often yields a low-quality fine-tuning training set (e.g., incorrect plans or intermediate reasoning).

arxiv-2411-03742.title: Adaptive Consensus Gradients Aggregation for Scaled Distributed Training
arxiv-2411-03742.creator: Yoni Choukroun, Shlomi Azoulay, Pavel Kisilev
arxiv-2411-03742.description: Abstract Distributed machine learning has recently become a critical paradigm for training large models on vast datasets. We examine the stochastic optimization problem for deep learning within synchronous parallel computing environments under communication constraints. While averaging distributed gradients is the most widely used method for gradient estimation, whether this is the optimal strategy remains an open question.

arxiv-2501-13297.title: RAMQA: A Unified Framework for Retrieval-Augmented Multi-Modal Question Answering
arxiv-2501-13297.creator: Yang Bai, Christan Grant, Daisy Zhe Wang
arxiv-2501-13297.description: Abstract Multi-modal retrieval-augmented Question Answering (MRAQA), integrating text and images, has gained significant attention in information retrieval (IR) and natural language processing (NLP). Traditional ranking methods rely on small encoder-based language models, which are incompatible with modern decoder-based generative large language models (LLMs) that have advanced various NLP tasks.

arxiv-2508-18741.title: Stability and Generalization for Bellman Residuals
arxiv-2508-18741.creator: Enoch H. Kang University of Washington, Kyoungseok Jang Chung-Ang University
arxiv-2508-18741.description: Abstract Offline reinforcement learning and offline inverse reinforcement learning aim to recover near–optimal value functions or reward models from a fixed batch of logged trajectories, yet current practice still struggles to enforce Bellman consistency. Bellman residual minimization (BRM) has emerged as an attractive remedy, as a globally convergent stochastic gradient descent–ascent based method for BRM has been recently discovered.

pmc-11478703.title: Vitamin D Supplementation Does Not Enhance Gains in Muscle Strength and Lean Body Mass or Influence Cardiorespiratory Fitness in Vitamin D-Insufficient Middle-Aged Men Engaged in Resistance Training
pmc-11478703.creator: Lauri Savolainen, Saima Timpmann, Martin Mooses, Evelin Mäestu, Luule Medijainen, Märt Lellsaar, Kristi Tiimann, Anneli Piir, Mihkel Zilmer, Eve Unt, Vahur Ööpik
pmc-11478703.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: This study checked whether vitamin D (Vit-D) supplementation improves the efficacy of resistance training (RT) in terms of increasing muscle strength and lean body mass (LBM), and influencing cardiorespiratory fitness (VO2max) in Vit-D-deficient middle-aged healthy men. Methods: Participants (n = 28) were quasi-randomly assigned to one of two groups, which, in a double-blind manner, supplemented their diet daily with either Vit-D (8000 IU; VD) or placebo (PLC) during participation in a 12-week supervised RT program.

pmc-11610930.title: Classifying the molecular functions of transcription factors beyond activation and repression
pmc-11610930.creator: Jinhong Dong, Michael J Guertin
pmc-11610930.description: In this Outlook, Dong and Guertin discuss a study in this issue of Genes & Development by Rogers et al. that provides mechanistic insight into target gene activation by the transcription factor Notch. They highlight the importance of temporal and scalable approaches to study, at a genome-wide resolution, transcription factor function and interactions that control transcription.

pmc-12649658.title: Polyphenol-Loaded Nanodevices as Innovative Therapeutic Strategies for Dry Eye Disease: Advances and Perspectives
pmc-12649658.creator: Raffaele Conte, Ilenia De Luca, Anna Calarco, Mauro Finicelli, Gianfranco Peluso
pmc-12649658.description: Background: Dry Eye Disease (DED) is a multifactorial ocular disorder characterized by tear film instability, inflammation, oxidative stress, and ocular surface damage. Current therapeutic options often provide only temporary relief and are limited by poor patient compliance and inadequate drug retention at the ocular surface.

pmc-13065480.title: Non-random patterns in the co-occurrence and accumulation of adverse life events in two national panel datasets
pmc-13065480.creator: Kyra Evers, Denny Borsboom, Eiko Fried, Fred Hasselman, František Bartoš, Lourens Waldorp
pmc-13065480.description: Adverse life events (ALEs), such as illness, bereavement, and accidents, can have profound consequences for physical and mental health. Although existing research highlights risk factors for ALEs, such as personality and socioeconomic status, less is known about patterns in ALEs themselves. How do events cluster and accumulate over time?

pmc-13348527.title: Role of Surgical Stabilization in the Management of Post-discectomy Septic Spondylodiscitis: Two Successful Case Reports
pmc-13348527.creator: G M Shafeeq, Mohammed Faizan, Paresh Bang
pmc-13348527.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Introduction:Spondylodiscitis is an inflammation (most commonly due to infection) involving the intervertebral disc and adjacent vertebral bodies. It represents a serious spinal condition that can lead to vertebral destruction, spinal instability, neurological deficits, and significant morbidity. Although the primary treatment consists of targeted antibiotic therapy and immobilization, surgical intervention becomes necessary in cases associated with spinal instability, neurological compromise, or failure of conservative treatment.

pmc-13439140.description: BackgroundExtrafascial interscalene block has been proposed to reduce phrenic nerve involvement while maintaining analgesic efficacy for shoulder surgery. However, a reproducible continuous catheter technique using a clear anatomical landmark has not been well described.CaseWe describe a case series of six patients undergoing shoulder surgery who received a continuous extrafascial interscalene block using the C6 transverse process as a bony landmark.

pmc-13469053.title: Polymorphic Transformation and Dislocation Regulation in MoS2 Enabled by Electric Field Postprocessing for Enhanced Electromagnetic Wave Absorption
pmc-13469053.creator: Xiangdong Wang, Zijing Li, Shengchong Hui, Hongjing Wu, Jiaming Wen, Limin Zhang
pmc-13469053.description: Highlights A direct current electric field postprocessing strategy enables precise control over the electronic structure and phase ratio of MoS2. Dislocation induced dipole arrays synergize with sulfur vacancies to enhance dipole polarization.Synergizing multiple loss mechanisms at 6 V for 10 min delivers an effective absorption bandwidth of 6.72 GHz, a 440% enhancement over the untreated sample.

pmc-13614363.title: Artificial Intelligence Should Not Prescribe Alone: A Risk-Stratified Pharmacy Governance Framework for Agentic Clinical Systems
pmc-13614363.creator: Esteban Zavaleta-Monestel, José A Castro-Gamboa, Jeaustin Mora-Jiménez

uslaw-usc-t42-s12901.title: 42 U.S.C. § 12901 — Purpose
uslaw-usc-t42-s12901.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t42-s12901.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 131 (Housing Opportunities For Persons With Aids). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The purpose of this chapter 1 is to provide States and localities with the resources and incentives to devise long-term comprehensive strategies for meeting the housing needs of persons with acquired immunodeficiency syndrome and families of such persons.
